device.name: OSRAM Lightify Gateway (+ paired Zigbee bulbs/plugs)
device.notes:
The Lightify Gateway is OSRAM's Wi-Fi-to-Zigbee bridge for its Lightify smart bulbs, strips and plugs. OSRAM shut the Lightify cloud on 2026-08-31 (2021 in the original announcement window), ending internet control, Alexa/Google integrations and — by several community reports — the ability to add devices or edit groups/scenes/timers through the app. OSRAM stated local Wi-Fi app control continues if the app is > 2.1.0 and the gateway Wi-Fi firmware is > 1.8.3.0. This is exactly the rescue case: the reverse-engineered local TCP protocol is the only fully-functional path left, and the bulbs behind it are plain Zigbee that any coordinator can also adopt.
TRANSPORT: a persistent TCP connection to gateway port 4000, binary, no authentication, no multiplexing (one outstanding request per connection). All multi-byte values little-endian; strings UTF-8.
FRAMING: bytes 0-1 packet length (excluding these two); byte 2 flag (0x00 unicast-to-device / 0x01 device-response / 0x02 broadcast-to-zone / 0x03 zone-response); byte 3 command id; bytes 4-7 a monotonically increasing request id. Responses insert a status byte at offset 8. Addressing: 8 bytes — a device is its uint64 MAC; a zone is the zone id in bytes 0-1, rest zero.
COMMANDS:
  0x13 list paired devices   0x1E list zones/groups   0x1F list scenes
  0x31 set brightness        0x32 set power on/off     0x33 set color temp (2000-6500 K)
  0x36 set RGBW color        0x52 activate scene       0x68 get device info
  0x6F get gateway firmware version
Each works per-device or per-zone via the flag + addressing scheme.

openness.notes: The gateway protocol is not published by OSRAM; noctarius reverse- engineered the binary format and python-lightify implements it. Post- shutdown provisioning behaviour is uncertain — sources disagree on whether new devices can still be added after the cloud closed.

credentials.notes: Local TCP 4000 control is unauthenticated on the LAN. Onboarding was cloud-mediated and is not documented here.

factory_reset.effect: A reset would clear the gateway's Zigbee network and Wi-Fi config. With the cloud gone, a reset risks stranding the gateway (re-onboarding may need the dead app); the reset gesture is not documented here.

cloud.local_alternative: Yes for control of already-paired devices — the TCP 4000 binary protocol drives them with no cloud. Adding NEW devices after the cloud shutdown is uncertain; the durable rescue is to re-pair the (plain Zigbee) bulbs to any Zigbee coordinator instead.

methods.description: Initial gateway onboarding and device pairing historically ran through the Lightify app and cloud. Post-shutdown, local control of already- paired devices works over TCP 4000; new-device pairing may require the (now-dead) cloud.

steps.action: Ensure the gateway carries final firmware (Wi-Fi firmware > 1.8.3.0).
Connect to gateway TCP 4000 and enumerate paired devices (0x13) / zones (0x1E).

setup.notes: Original onboarding used the Lightify app + cloud. After the 2026-08-31 shutdown, adding new devices reportedly no longer works while already- paired local control survives; the gateway must carry final firmware (Wi-Fi firmware > 1.8.3.0). Provisioning wire steps are not documented here.

rejoin.notes: No documented local Wi-Fi re-provisioning path; with the cloud down, moving the gateway to a new network is risky. Re-pairing the bulbs to a standalone Zigbee coordinator is the more durable option.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The binary framing, command ids and port 4000 are from noctarius/lightify-binary-protocol, corroborated on the port by python-lightify.
